rules.correspondence: One directed edge per archival item from each named sender to each named recipient. Copies, drafts, telegrams, excerpts, enclosures and form slips all count as attestations that A wrote to B. Offices (o_*) stand for unnamed signers.
rules.stated: A relation asserted inside a document by its writer (partner, friend, officer of the same company, familiar salutation, recommendation, request). Each edge carries the quotation that asserts it and the date of the document that carries the quotation. The date is the document's, not the relationship's. Letterhead officer lists are printed, not written by the signer; such ties are tagged letterhead.
rules.pi: A relation asserted in the principal investigator's own writing (Cast of Characters, Tale §3, timeline summaries). Kept separate because it is interpretation, not attestation; PI ties are undated.
rules.affiliation: Person to institution. Each edge carries one quotation that names the person in that institution (status 'stated'), or is marked 'inferred' where the model read the affiliation from context; inferred affiliations are drawn dashed and listed separately. Letterhead attestations are tagged letterhead.
rules.funding: A funding edge exists only where a provided text states a sum or a promise of one; amounts are as written; no total is computed.
rules.coattestation: Derived by counting the existing edges per pair; it adds no tie.
rules.mentions: Derived automatically by name-variant matching on the transcription text (model); not an asserted tie; recall is incomplete.
rules.exclusions: No tie is inferred from co-mention, shared location, or outside knowledge. Mentions are indexed per document and shown only as a layer labelled derived; they are not asserted ties.

views.label: Persons
views.node: persons, unnamed offices and institutions (circles; offices dashed)
views.rule: A tie exists only where a provided text asserts it; the four kinds of evidence are kept apart and can be shown separately.
caveats: Node size and degree describe the surviving file, not the historical world: a person whose letters were not kept has a low degree.

views.label: Institutions
views.node: persons (circles) and institutions (squares sized by the persons attested in them)

views.rule: Person to institution. Each edge carries one quotation that names the person in that institution (status 'stated'), or is marked 'inferred' where the model read the affiliation from context; inferred affiliations are drawn dashed and listed separately. Letterhead attestations are tagged letterhead.
caveats: An 'inferred' affiliation is the model's reading of context, not a statement in the file; the institution's place may itself be inferred (place_status).

views.label: Funding
views.node: funders · the Museum fund · the expeditions · the field (Quackenbush; Quinn)
views.edge: a stated sum or promise, labelled with the amount as written; status as dash pattern
views.rule: A funding edge exists only where a provided text states a sum or a promise of one; amounts are as written; no total is computed.
caveats: Sturgis's $250 is 'a contribution toward the field exploration fund of your Department'; the file does not say it was for the mammoth.
The 1909 halves ($856.14 each) and the stated total ($1,712.27) differ by one cent; registered as a discrepancy.
The Tale's 'just over $1,600' and present-value figures are the PI's, not attested sums.
Pyne's January 1909 cheque ('Pls find check.') and the Trustees' thanks of 14 November 1907 name no sum and are not drawn.

views.label: Co-attestation

views.rule: Derived by counting the existing edges per pair; it adds no tie.
caveats: Co-attestation measures the surviving file, not the strength of a historical relationship; a kind count of 1 means one surviving voice, not a weak tie.

caveats: A mention is a name in the text, not a relationship; senders and recipients are excluded; the matching guards are stated in each document's mentions_method.
